Discrete Morse gives integral wedge of 33 S^2. The frozen verifier additionally specifies independent 2^20 membership tests, boundary ranks (19,111,176,44), all 240 orientation-signed Lefschetz traces, seven cycle-type pairs and Murnaghan–Nakayama inner products; the trace algorithm and character decomposition were inspected in source but not independently reexecuted in full. The identity trace 33, transpose trace 9, ± dimensions 21 and 12 and absence of full invariants follow from the documented complete certificate plus Lefschetz theorem. Pure dimension four, non-top degree homology rules out shellability.

value.rationale: Five-crown is a canonical dense bipartite graph obtained from K5,5 by removing a 1-factor. Its perfect-matching complex tests the topological effect of extendibility beyond ordinary matching complexes, and the nontrivial 240-element symmetry representation is a natural invariant, not merely a count of derangements. The 33-sphere wedge and two distinct central involution eigenspaces are meaningful complete facts for the first four-regular crown case.
